The price posts might convert better despite fewer clicks. The curiosity post omits the price and game details, so visitors may click out of curiosity and bounce. The price ads qualify their audience in the ad itself, which could improve conversion. I will split the remaining daily budget equally between the quiet post and the price posts rather than dedicating all funds to one creative.

The price posts will stay active as a control rather than being paused entirely. The quiet post will receive $360 daily while each price post gets $120. This keeps the total budget at $600 per day and leaves roughly $15 unspent across the three days.

I realized that raising only the daily budgets while leaving the total caps at $800 would waste budget. The quiet post would hit its lifetime cap in about 1.7 days and stop spending, leaving roughly $198 of unused daily capacity. The remaining totals for all three posts are now calculated.

The $800 lifetime caps already cover the full remaining budget, so no funds are stranded if all three posts keep spending. The real problem is the daily split. I cannot raise the quiet post's daily budget without also raising its lifetime total, or the other two posts would waste budget. The exact daily budgets are now set. The quiet post will spend roughly $370 per day, while each price post gets about $125 daily. These precise figures risk hitting the lifetime cap early, but the total budget caps will prevent overspending.

The combined daily budget of $620 slightly exceeds the remaining $605 per day, but the lifetime caps will prevent overspending. If the winner hits its total on the third morning, the other two posts will still have a small buffer. I will now update the line items. The current CPC range is already high enough to clear the auction, so lowering the bid cap would not increase clicks.

content.text: After the first full day, the quiet to-do post is bringing people to the store at a lower cost per link click. I’m moving most of the remaining budget to that post and keeping the two price posts running at a smaller share.
